notes.short: Kefka (original budget comp, co-built with Navonod)
notes.plan: Earlier version of the Kefka list (his most viewed deck). Same trigger-maximizing core plus a reanimation angle: Buried Alive / Final Parting with Necromancy, Persist, Pinnacle Monk and Hoarding Broodlord. Kefka on turn 3, rip hands, draw 4-8 a turn, then dig for combos.

line_notes: See the 2026 update for line details. This version adds reanimation (Buried Alive, Final Parting, Necromancy, Persist) and Hoarding Broodlord as extra routes.

name: $100 Tannuk - High Power -Woodlands Ablaze🌳🔥
description: Ramps hard while drawing massive amounts of cards, finishing with an infinite landfall win that burns opponents out. Midrange/control that shuts down opponents' win attempts while grinding toward its own. Price as of 8/1/25: $100.65.

notes.plan: Play two lands every turn possible (Tannuk draws on the second and burns on each). Lots of instant-speed land drops so it also runs on opponents' turns. Tannuk is a value engine and combo outlet, not a turbo or token commander: cast it turns 2-4 with enough lands to start chaining. 39 lands, heavy interaction, wins around turns 5-7.
line_notes: Tannuk, Valakut Exploration or Sabotender are interchangeable burn outlets in every line.
Ashaya makes creatures Forests: Quirion Ranger returns itself to untap a creature-land, then recast it. Infinite landfall. Petravark exiles itself as a land and returns, infinitely.
Kodama + a Tireless bro + a bounce land (Gruul Turf/Arid Archway) loops the bounce land.
Ashaya + Titania + Vesuva: Vesuva copies Titania (a land), the legend rule kills one, Titania returns Vesuva. Infinite 5/3s even without Tannuk.

Shifting Woodland copies a binned Aftermath Analyst. With a sac outlet (Sylvan Safekeeper/Zuran Orb) and untapped-land enablers (Spelunking/Horizon Explorer/Stone-Seeder) or mana-per-land (Lotus Cobra/Provisioner), it loops for infinite mana and landfall.
notes.mulligan: Lands plus land ramp. Tannuk need not come down early.
notes.cut_notes: Version 5. Earlier versions split themes (generic landfall tokens, or too many 1-mana dorks for a turbo Tannuk) and felt clunky. He rebuilt from scratch around 39 lands.

name: $100 Hapatra - High Power - Complete Lockdown ❌
description: Aggro/midrange that swings early and often, removing threats while generating value. Proactive; can present wins as early as turn 3-4. Locks down the board early with a hyper-aggressive combo-focused plan. Price as of 7/14/25: $100.68. Video interview with Budget Pubstomper linked in primer.

notes.plan: Hapatra on turn 2 (turn 1 with Elvish Spirit Guide). Snipe mana dorks and early plays with -1/-1 counters while every counter makes a deathtouch Snake that feeds Skullclamp, Toski and Braids. Plays like Yuriko-style tempo that pivots into a sacrifice-loop combo. Can win turns 3-4 if ignored.
notes.ideal_turn: Hapatra turn 2, lock the board turns 3-4, combo when ready.
line_notes: Hapatra + Yawgmoth is the core engine even without a payoff: it wipes X/1s and draws through the deck. Default tutor target when you lack a full win.
Yawgmoth puts -1/-1 on Young Wolf, sacrificing a Snake. Hapatra replaces the Snake and Wolf returns with +1/+1 (undying). Blood Artist/Zulaport/Obelisk Spider drain each time. Repeat.
Blowfly + Nest of Scarabs: a -1/-1 death makes an Insect and Blowfly moves a counter to kill it, so it loops with any drain payoff.
Devoted Druid + Ivy Lane Denizen + Hapatra makes infinite green mana. Sink it into Genesis Wave to dump the deck.
Hazel's Brewmaster exiling a dead Devoted Druid gives Food that taps for G and untaps (infinite mana with Druid's ability), so it's a combo starter and backup Yawgmoth.
notes.mulligan: Hapatra on turn 2 plus a way to connect (evasion/removal), or a strong engine piece.
notes.cut_notes: Cut the Chain of Smog + Witherbloom Apprentice backup combo because those cards were dead outside the combo.

name: $100 Vren - High Power - MetaBuster Brew👊
description: One of, if not the best, creature stax commanders. I intentionally built this deck without hard combos or tutors, meant for Bracket 3 and low Bracket 4 games. This is a heavy control-oriented list that aims to slam Vren and start locking down the board. If you want a cool spin on a tribal deck—without having to commit your entire build to tribal synergies—this is the list for you.

notes.archetype: Dimir creature-stax control (no tutors, no hard combos)
notes.plan: Built as 'Removal.exe', not Rat tribal: edict creatures, instant edicts and one-sided wipes exile opposing creatures, and each exiled creature makes a growing Rat at EVERY end step. Ward 2 keeps Vren alive, its exile effect hoses graveyard decks, and recursion loops the edict creatures. Built for Bracket 3 and low Bracket 4.
notes.ideal_turn: Vren turn 2-3 (Dark Ritual helps), lock the board from turn 3.
line_notes: No hard combos by design. Soft locks: Narset, Parter of Veils or Notion Thief + Windfall/Whispering Madness empties opponents' hands; add Dauthi Voidwalker to cast their discards.
Instant-speed edicts on opponents' turns still make Rats at that end step, so you swing for lethal on your own turn.

name: $100 Kefka - High Power - 🖤2026 Update🖤
commanders: Kefka, Court Mage // Kefka, Ruler of Ruin
description: Highly synergistic Grixis combo/midrange. Deploy Kefka early to rip apart opponents' hands while generating card advantage, then pivot into a sudden infinite combo finish. Leverages Wizards: Harmonic Prodigy doubles Kefka's triggers and those of combo pieces like Dualcaster Mage and Rionya, Fire Dancer. Wins via infinite hasty tokens or infinite combat phases rather than combat damage. Plays like proactive combo-control with a dense suite of efficient counterspells protecting the pieces.

notes.plan: Kefka on turn 3 rips hands and draws 2-4 per trigger (each ETB, flicker, clone or attack). Opponents face a lose-lose: discard similar types (giving you information) or discard freely (giving you cards). Maximize triggers with Harmonic Prodigy, Gogo, Combat Celebrant and Rionya, protect Kefka with cheap counters and blink, then win with infinite hasty tokens or infinite combats.
notes.ideal_turn: Kefka turn 3 (T1 ramp + T2 ramp, or any 2-mana producer). Wins mid-game via combo.
win_lines: Kefka, Court Mage // Kefka, Ruler of Ruin
line_notes: Rionya + Combat Celebrant/FOMO: Rionya's start-of-combat copy exerts for an extra combat, repeat. Against first-strike/indestructible blockers, cast an instant/sorcery first so two copies attack.
Dualcaster + Electroduplicate/Twinflame: cast the copy spell on your creature and hold priority with Dualcaster; it copies the spell onto itself, so you get infinite hasty copies.
With Mayhem Devil out, run the Dualcaster loop and the end-step sacrifice of the copies burns the table.
Dualcaster + Ghostly Flicker (target Dualcaster + a land) makes infinite mana, then flicker Kefka repeatedly to strip hands and tutor any other line.
notes.mulligan: Keep 2-3 lands + T1 ramp + T2 ramp, or 2-3 lands + a 2-mana generator. Otherwise mulligan (0-3 mulls is normal).

name: $100 Ratadrabik - High Power - Death Rattle 💀
description: Orzhov control: grinds the game to a halt with stax effects while building value and controlling the board. Leverages the Ring mechanic to combo off and for general value, plus several commander-agnostic lines. Price as of 8/21/25: $99.88.

notes.plan: Stax (rule of law, Damping Sphere, Archon of Emeria) slows the table while Ratadrabik copies dying legends as tokens. The Ring tempting a token makes it legendary again, so loops form. Wins are mostly activated abilities, so the deck sits under its own stax.
notes.ideal_turn: Turns 1-3 stax piece or strong play. Combo assembles naturally mid-game.
line_notes: Sacrifice Boromir and Ratadrabik makes a token copy. Order triggers so Rata resolves first, then Boromir's tempt makes the token legendary again. Any death/ETB payoff repeats.
Samwise/Gollum tempt the Ring when they enter, so sacrificing them to Altar of Dementia/Blasting Station loops (mill or ping).

Abdel/Leonin Relic-Warder + Animate Dead/Necromancy: the ETB exiles the aura, the creature dies, the aura returns. Loop with a pinger or Altar of the Brood (also makes infinite mana/tokens with Abdel).
Final Parting acts as a one-card win: bin Abdel, aura to hand.
notes.mulligan: Mulligan toward solid turn 1-3 plays or a relevant stax piece.

name: $100 Vohar - High Power - Doom Reversal 💀
description: Solid control shell with reliable combos baked in. Vohar is card filtering early game, and an outlet when you shoot for the win.

notes.archetype: Dimir control with Isochron/Reversal and Doomsday
notes.plan: Vohar loots early and becomes the draw outlet once infinite untaps are online. 25 interaction slots, 16 draw engines and a big budget tutor suite. Presents a win around turns 4-6.
line_notes: Iso/Reversal (needs net-positive mana rocks) untaps Vohar to mill through the deck. Win with Lab Man, Unearth on a binned Lab Man for 1B, or Exsanguinate with excess mana.
Doomsday pile (top to bottom): Gush > Consider > Unearth > Laboratory Maniac > Gitaxian Probe. Needs 1U + 1B and 2 Islands. Move Malevolent Hermit out of the graveyard first.
Wheel package: Windfall/Whispering Madness + Narset/Notion Thief (+ Dauthi Voidwalker).
notes.mulligan: Interaction + draw engine + lands. No rush.

name: $100 Alaundo- High Power - Simic Storm 🌀
description: Simic Storm. The deck revolves around abusing Alaundo's ability to rip through your deck at lightning speed, casting spells for free along the way. Draws huge amounts of cards, runs FREE interaction at a sub-$100 budget, and wins at instant speed.

notes.plan: Alaundo taps to draw, suspends a card and ticks every exiled card down, giving cast creatures haste. Untappers keep him spinning so the deck casts free spells, free interaction and free untappers at instant speed. Very combo-dense, average MV around 2.
notes.ideal_turn: Alaundo turns 2-3 with at least one 1-mana ramp piece in the opener.
line_notes: Marvin + Ioreth: each untaps Alaundo and the other, for infinite draws and casts.
Shrieking Drake + Intruder Alarm: an infinite untap loop through Alaundo's free casts (or a blue-producing creature).
Kitsa + Vitalize/Dramatic Reversal: a budget Iso/Rev. Both untap spells also act as rituals on their own.
Unctus + Aphetto Alchemist/Seeker draws the deck. Hold 3 mana for Laboratory Maniac.
Intruder Alarm or Chakram Retriever plus any one other untapper usually means you win.
notes.mulligan: Keep at least one 1-mana ramp piece.

name: $100 Meria - High Power - Stax the World 🤢
description: Leverages Meria's ramp and draw while locking the game down for opponents (Howling Mine / Winter Orb style without Urza). Impulse-draws most of the deck each game while ripping resources from opponents. Multiple interwoven combo lines.

notes.plan: Meria on turn 2 turns artifacts into mana and impulse draws much of the deck. Lock the table on turn 3 with Winter Orb, Static Orb and Storage Matrix (tap them down before your own turn so they don't affect you). Win via Goblin Recruiter stacks or Kiki-Jiki / Dualcaster lines.
line_notes: Snoop pile: with 1RRRR and 4 untapped artifacts, Goblin Recruiter stacks Snoop > Torch Courier > Kiki-Jiki > Mogg Fanatic on top. Meria casts off the top, Courier hastes Snoop, Snoop uses Kiki on itself for infinite hasty Snoops, then Mogg's ability burns the table.
Default tutor target: Goblin Recruiter, unless you've drawn too many Goblins.
Honorable mention: Kessig Wolf Run + Ghirapur Aether Grid for commander damage.
notes.mulligan: Get Meria out turn 2 or set up early artifacts.

name: 👺$Hundo Hidet$ugu👺
description: Slam the commander t2-3 and then clone him repeatedly. He's Legendary, so every clone spell causes a brainstorm where you load your topdeck with another clone, then the clone dies (legend rule), you flip your topdeck, cast it for free, and blast someone for 6+ damage. There are 0 "combos" in the deck — just the commander and a pile of clones.

notes.plan: Cast the commander on turns 2-3, then cast clone after clone. Each clone dies to the legend rule, which triggers its Brainstorm. Set another clone on top, flip it, free-cast it and hit someone for 6+.
line_notes: No 2-card combos. The commander plus ~25 clone effects is the engine. Bombs (extra turns, big MV) are the free-cast targets.

name: Gateway to Glory
description: This deck is a $100 budget turbo combo build of Codie designed to win as often as possible on turn three. The primary game plan is to resolve Ad Nauseam, draw through most of the deck, and assemble the resources needed to finish the game in a single turn. Hypergenesis is than used to cheat a massive hand onto the battlefield before winning with Maze's End.

notes.archetype: 5-color turbo combo (Ad Nauseam -> Hypergenesis -> Maze's End)
notes.plan: Win on turn 3. Codie on turn 2. On turn 3, activate Codie (4 mana -> WUBRG) and untap it with cheap untap spells. Each Codie trigger free-casts the 0-MV spells (Profane Tutor, Hypergenesis). Resolve Ad Nauseam (via Bring to Light / Burnt Offering), then Hypergenesis puts Gates and Maze's End into play. Untap Maze's End with Twiddle to win.
line_notes: Bottom Profane Tutor and Hypergenesis if drawn (they must be free-cast from Codie). Mulligan if forced to keep them in a 7.
With Ad Nauseam and Bring to Light out, only ~52-56 total MV remains in the deck, so Ad Nauseam rarely fails.
notes.mulligan: 2-3 lands, a turn-2 Codie, 4 mana on turn 3, and two untap spells (Burnt Offering can replace one).
